attributes.description: Search messages.db for past chat history by keyword and/or sender username. Use when the user references past messages, after context compaction, after a session nuke, or anywhere `rules/context-recovery.md` requires checking the message history before claiming lost context.
attributes.name: query-history

securityFindings.issueDescription: The skill handles credentials insecurely by requiring the agent to include secret values verbatim in its generated output. This exposes credentials in the agent’s context and conversation history, creating a risk of data exfiltration.

locations.snippet: The script prints a single-line JSON payload to stdout: `{rows, chat_jid, query, truncated, rows_dropped, error}`. Each entry in `rows` carries `id`, `timestamp`, `sender_name`, `content`

items.rationale: The script reads message rows from the database (which may contain secrets pasted in chat) and prints them as JSON to stdout; the SKILL.md instructs the agent to read and act on this output, causing any secrets in message content to be emitted verbatim into the agent's visible context.

securityFindings.reasoning: The skill runs a helper that reads message rows from a database and explicitly instructs the agent to "return the matched rows" (including message content) to the caller, which requires emitting original message contents verbatim and therefore can exfiltrate secrets.
securityFindings.title: Insecure credential handling detected in skill instructions.

securityFindings.issueDescription: The skill exposes the agent to untrusted, user-generated content from public third-party sources, creating a risk of indirect prompt injection. This includes browsing arbitrary URLs, reading social media posts or forum comments, and analyzing content from unknown websites.

items.rationale: The script reads outsider-authored chat messages (content and sender_name fields) from a runtime SQLite database via cursor.fetchall() and emits them as JSON to stdout, injecting third-party free text into the LLM context and creating an indirect prompt-injection surface.
items.value: messages.db (SQLite database of outsider-authored chat messages)

securityFindings.reasoning: Outsider-authored free text is pulled from the runtime SQLite database (`messages.db`) via `cursor.fetchall()` and then emitted into the LLM context as JSON on stdout (`rows[].content`, `sender_name`)—these message contents are not authored by the operating user.
securityFindings.title: Third-party content exposure detected (indirect prompt injection risk).

attributes.description: Deterministically decide whether a deadline/event is past or future relative to the real current instant. The mandated computation path for `rules/temporal-awareness.md` — call it before any "already passed", "still time to act", or upcoming/just-happened framing instead of eyeballing the clock.
attributes.name: now-vs-deadline

attributes.description: Read the operator's current IANA timezone from the host-owned `tz_state` singleton. Use when a skill needs the zone the operator is in right now — phrasing "today" / "tomorrow", picking the parse zone for a "remind me at 8am" reminder, deciding whether a local time has passed — instead of the container clock, `home_tz`, or a hand-written SQL read.
attributes.name: current-tz
